rows.title: Affective Behaviour Analysis of On-line User Interactions: Are On-line Support Groups more Therapeutic than Twitter?
rows.question: How did they obtain the OSG dataset?
rows.gold_answer: crawling and pre-processing an OSG web forum
rows.our_answer: By “crawling and pre-processing an OSG web forum.”
rows.judge_reason: The candidate exactly matches the gold answer.

rows.title: External Lexical Information for Multilingual Part-of-Speech Tagging
rows.question: which languages are explored?
rows.gold_answer: Bulgarian, Croatian, Czech, Danish, English, French, German, Indonesian, Italian, Norwegian, Persian, Polish, Portuguese, Slovenian, Spanish and Swedish
rows.our_answer: Bulgarian, Croatian, Czech, Danish, English, French, German, Indonesian, Italian, Norwegian, Persian, Polish, Portuguese, Slovenian, Spanish, and Swedish.
rows.judge_reason: The candidate lists exactly the same sixteen languages as the gold answer.

rows.title: Paraphrase-Supervised Models of Compositionality
rows.question: Which translation systems do they compare against?
rows.gold_answer: hierarchical phrase-based system BIBREF29; appropriate additional baseline would be to mark translation rules with these indicator functions but without the scores, akin to identifying rules with phrases in them (Baseline + SegOn)
rows.our_answer: A hierarchical phrase-based baseline system with a 4-gram language model, tuned using MIRA.
rows.judge_reason: It mentions only the hierarchical phrase-based baseline and omits the additional Baseline + SegOn comparison system.

rows.title: Macaw: An Extensible Conversational Information Seeking Platform
rows.question: What interface does Macaw currently have?
rows.gold_answer: File IO; Standard IO; Telegram
rows.our_answer: A command-line interface and mobile, desktop, and web apps, including a Telegram bot.
rows.judge_reason: It omits File IO and incorrectly adds mobile, desktop, and web apps.

rows.title: Attention Is All You Need for Chinese Word Segmentation
rows.question: What is meant by closed test setting?
rows.gold_answer: closed test limits all the data for learning should not be beyond the given training set, while open test does not take this limitation
rows.our_answer: “Closed test limits all the data for learning [to] not be beyond the given training set.”
rows.judge_reason: The candidate correctly states that a closed test restricts learning data to the given training set.

rows.title: Follow Alice into the Rabbit Hole: Giving Dialogue Agents Understanding of Human Level Attributes.
rows.question: How does dataset model character's profiles?
rows.gold_answer: attributes are determined by human viewers and their impressions of the characters, and are correlated with human-like characteristics
rows.our_answer: By combining detailed Human Level Attribute (HLA) data with dialogue data for specific characters.
rows.judge_reason: The candidate describes combining attribute and dialogue data, not that profiles are based on viewers' impressions and correlated with human-like characteristics.

rows.title: Symmetric Regularization based BERT for Pair-wise Semantic Reasoning
rows.question: How much is performance improved on NLI?
rows.gold_answer: improvement on the RTE dataset is significant, i.e., 4% absolute gain over the BERTBase
rows.our_answer: “4% absolute gain over the BERTBase” on the RTE dataset.
rows.judge_reason: The candidate exactly matches the reported 4% absolute gain over BERTBase on RTE.

rows.title: Dice Loss for Data-imbalanced NLP Tasks
rows.question: What are method's improvements of F1 w.r.t. baseline BERT tagger for Chinese POS datasets?
rows.gold_answer: +1.86 in terms of F1 score on CTB5; +1.80 on CTB6; +2.19 on UD1.4
rows.our_answer: +1.86 on CTB5, +1.80 on CTB6, and +2.19 on UD1.4.
rows.judge_reason: The candidate exactly matches the reported F1 improvements for CTB5, CTB6, and UD1.4.

rows.title: Topic Identification for Speech without ASR
rows.question: How is the vocabulary of word-like or phoneme-like units automatically discovered?
rows.gold_answer: Zero Resource Toolkit (ZRTools) BIBREF7
rows.our_answer: By unsupervised term discovery (UTD) using segmental DTW for word-like units, or Variational Bayesian HMM-based acoustic unit discovery (AUD) for phoneme-like units.
rows.judge_reason: The candidate describes discovery methods but does not identify the Zero Resource Toolkit (ZRTools) named in the gold answer.

rows.title: Improving Neural Text Simplification Model with Simplified Corpora
rows.question: what are the sizes of both datasets?
rows.gold_answer: training set has 89,042 sentence pairs, and the test set has 100 pairs; training set contains 296,402; 2,000 for development and 359 for testing
rows.our_answer: WikiSmall: 89,042 training pairs and 100 test pairs; WikiLarge: 296,402 training pairs, plus 2,000 development and 359 test sentences, each with 8 simplifications.
rows.judge_reason: The candidate accurately reports the training, development, and test sizes for both WikiSmall and WikiLarge.

rows.title: Cross-lingual Pre-training Based Transfer for Zero-shot Neural Machine Translation
rows.question: which datasets did they experiment with?
rows.gold_answer: Europarl; MultiUN
rows.our_answer: Europarl and MultiUN.
rows.judge_reason: The candidate names both datasets in the gold answer: Europarl and MultiUN.

rows.title: Multilingual Sentiment Analysis: An RNN-Based Framework for Limited Data
rows.question: which non-english language had the best performance?
rows.gold_answer: Russian
rows.our_answer: Russian, with 85.62% accuracy.
rows.judge_reason: The candidate correctly identifies Russian as the best-performing non-English language.

rows.title: A BERT-Based Transfer Learning Approach for Hate Speech Detection in Online Social Media
rows.question: What existing approaches do they compare to?
rows.gold_answer: Waseem and Hovy BIBREF5, Davidson et al. BIBREF9, and Waseem et al. BIBREF10
rows.our_answer: Waseem and Hovy, Davidson et al., and Waseem et al. baselines.
rows.judge_reason: The candidate names the same three prior approaches as the gold answer.

rows.title: Mining Supervisor Evaluation and Peer Feedback in Performance Appraisals
rows.question: What clustering algorithms were used?
rows.gold_answer: CLUTO; Carrot2 Lingo
rows.our_answer: CLUTO and Carrot2 Lingo.
rows.judge_reason: The candidate names both clustering algorithms: CLUTO and Carrot2 Lingo.

rows.title: Neural Collective Entity Linking
rows.question: How effective is their NCEL approach overall?
rows.gold_answer: NCEL consistently outperforms various baselines with a favorable generalization ability
rows.our_answer: NCEL “consistently outperforms various baselines” and state-of-the-art collective methods across five datasets, with favorable generalization and efficiency.
rows.judge_reason: The candidate matches the gold answer by stating that NCEL consistently outperforms baselines and has favorable generalization.

rows.title: A multi-layer approach to disinformation detection on Twitter
rows.question: How is the political bias of different sources included in the model?
rows.gold_answer: By assigning a political bias label to each news article and training only on left-biased or right-biased outlets of both disinformation and mainstream domains
rows.our_answer: By assigning political-bias labels to US outlets—and thus their articles—following the procedure in BIBREF2, then training only on left- or right-biased networks.
rows.judge_reason: It matches the gold answer by describing article-level bias labels and training restricted to left- or right-biased sources.

rows.title: Context-Aware Monolingual Repair for Neural Machine Translation
rows.question: by how much did the BLEU score improve?
rows.gold_answer: On average 0.64
rows.our_answer: 0.7 BLEU over the baseline and CADec.
rows.judge_reason: The candidate states a 0.7 BLEU improvement, while the gold answer specifies an average improvement of 0.64.

rows.title: On the effectiveness of feature set augmentation using clusters of word embeddings
rows.question: How were the cluster extracted?
rows.gold_answer: Word clusters are extracted using k-means on word embeddings
rows.our_answer: By clustering the embeddings with k-means, initialized using “k-means++” and run for 300 iterations.
rows.judge_reason: The candidate correctly states that clusters were extracted by applying k-means to word embeddings.

rows.title: What does Attention in Neural Machine Translation Pay Attention to?
rows.question: In what cases is attention different from alignment?
rows.gold_answer: For certain POS tags, e.g. VERB, PRON.
rows.our_answer: “In the case of verbs,” attention “captures other information rather than only the translational equivalent,” attending to “context words influencing the current word translation.”
rows.judge_reason: The candidate identifies verbs as a POS case where attention differs from alignment and explains the difference.

rows.title: High Quality ELMo Embeddings for Seven Less-Resourced Languages
rows.question: How larger are the training sets of these versions of ELMo compared to the previous ones?
rows.gold_answer: By 14 times.
rows.our_answer: “A few hundred million tokens” versus the previous “20-million token corpora.”
rows.judge_reason: A few hundred million tokens compared with 20 million implies an approximately 14-fold increase.
